title: Alzheimer’s Disease MRI Research
summary: A medical-imaging study using Python, OpenCV, and CNN ensembles to classify dementia severity and quantify brain atrophy from MRI scans.
landingDeck: A four-class MRI study that improved dementia-severity classification from 78% to 85% through CNN ensemble comparison and error analysis.
landingHighlights: Inspects representative MRI slices before preprocessing and training.
Trains a CNN across four disease-stage labels with the data split recorded in the notebook.
Compares CNN ensembles and model errors, improving measured classification accuracy from 78% to 85%.
problem: Medical imaging experiments can become difficult to judge when the final score is separated from the images, preprocessing choices, label structure, and evaluation path.
approach: The notebook keeps the study sequence visible: MRI inspection, image resizing, augmentation, four-class labeling, CNN training, and ensemble-oriented comparison.
output: A repository-backed Colab notebook and supporting image outputs that record the experiment as a reproducible sequence. It is a research study, not a clinical system.

methodology.evaluation: Four-class CNN baseline and ensemble models use an 80/10/10 split and are compared with held-out classification accuracy and recorded error analysis.
methodology.boundary: The study is an educational research experiment. It does not establish clinical validity, diagnostic performance, or readiness for patient care.

role: I built the data preparation, augmentation, training, and evaluation flow and preserved the notebook as the visible record of the experiment.

pageSections.title: The model predicts four disease-stage labels
pageSections.description: The classification target is more demanding than a simple healthy-versus-disease split.
pageSections.markdown:
The study uses four classes: NonDemented, VeryMildDemented, MildDemented, and ModerateDemented. The model must distinguish progression levels that can be visually close and unevenly represented.

The notebook carries this four-class setup through data preparation, augmentation, training, and evaluation. Ensemble comparison follows the recorded CNN baseline. The project is a reproducible experiment record; it does not claim clinical readiness.

pageSections.description: The contribution is a reproducible experimental method. The work is not a production or clinical system.
pageSections.markdown: This work records a practical medical-imaging workflow in one reproducible file: dataset preparation, convolutional modeling, four-class prediction, and ensemble evaluation. Reviewers can inspect, rerun, and extend each stage. The study does not establish clinical validity or deployment readiness.
